timeline.message:
Avoid port-scan in testThatTransportClientCanConnect

300 concurrent connection attempts, each with a 30s timeout, will take
way longer than is reasonable in a test. With this commit we connect
directly to addresses to which we know nodes are bound.
timeline.author: David Turner

timeline.body:
300 concurrent connection attempts, each with a 30s timeout, will take
way longer than is reasonable in a test. With this commit we connect
directly to addresses to which we know nodes are bound.

Closes #108627
Closes #109400
Is there any expectation for a minimum number of addresses that have been collected? Wondering if there's a sanity check that we are in fact testing some number of addresses.

reply.body: Yes every node must bind to at least one transport address, otherwise it wouldn't be able to join a cluster.

timeline.body: This seems to make sense.. `Netty4Plugin.getTransports` creates a `Netty4Transport`, which I think is the `Transport` type you're grabbing from each node. Then the implication seems to be that `Transport` holds all the addresses on which a node listens?

Is the idea here that prepareHealth broadcasts to all nodes / transport addresses? Are we tricking the TransportClient into thinking that each address is a different node? I see `transportClient.addTransportAddresses` eventually ends up [creating a list of DiscoveryNodes](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/d38e4b028f4a9784bb74de339ac1b877e2dbea6f/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/client/transport/TransportClientNodesService.java#L188-L199).

reply.body: No, the `TransportClient` ultimately chooses just one address to which to send the request.
